set: P9 people: townsfolk portraits, business icons, network/gate HUD icons, home sprites (spouse, babe, child, youth)

revisions.what: first P9 set: 16 portraits, business + HUD icons, home sprites (backup: src/people/build/rev1/)

faces: 5 structures spread so neighbours differ; town variants (every town: innkeeper, merchant, sweetheart); sweethearts -f / -m / neutral; cradle + held babe redrawn with faces; gate lamps 3x3 for 1x; Edda portrait + sprite agree (blue dress, white apron, ledger) and read against the Ashford boards; new verify checks

tier: 8-bit road/city tier: strict NES palette (reference/nes-palette.js), alpha 0/255, no anti-aliasing
portraitTierNote: Portraits are NES tier, not 16-bit: they only appear in the city People/Family/relationship UI over the 8-bit city scene and sit next to 8-bit walkers; ART-BRIEF section 1 groups "battle / portraits" as 16-bit, which we read as battle-side portraits (captain cards). A 16-bit townsfolk set would need Ronja's call (open question).

factionKeys.rule: no Warden key (G, n) anywhere in P9; Covenant keys only on Covenant-tagged assets; Nightglass keys only on Nightglass-tagged assets; League reads by gold + steel (Y/y/O + S/s/w), gold also appears as small neutral accents (coins, lamps, hair)

portraits.frame: 1 px K border + lit backdrop (light from the upper left, dark corner bottom right); crown row 10, skull centre x23, shoulders cut by the bottom edge
portraits.keyForm: pt-<role> with role ids from data/townsfolk.js ROLES (guildmaster = guild, Nightglass broker = broker); officials pt-official-<faction>; town variants pt-<town>-<role>
portraits.lookupNote: ui/folk.js portrait() tries pt-<town>-<role> then pt-<role>. Officials (role "official") have no pt-official file: add `pt-${n.role}-${n.faction}` between the two (n.faction is league/covenant/nightglass, contested towns draw a Nightglass official).
portraits.displayNote: native 48x48; crisp at 48 or 96 (the relationship screen draws 96 = 2x). The People list (38 px) and the Family panel (56 px) scale by non-integer factors: use 48 there, or set the texture filter to NEAREST. With art present the placeholder trusted/rival stroke is no longer drawn: stroke it over the image (a 2 px stroke at inset 1 covers only the frame and backdrop edge).

atlas.orderNote: rev 2 keeps the rev 1 order (16 cells) as a prefix; new portraits are appended

faces.what: rev 2: five face structures instead of one template. Each portrait entry carries `face`. Shared by all: crown row ~10-13, skull centre x23, midline x25 (the same 3/4 turn), light from the upper left

describe.A: oval: the rev 1 geometry, eyes mid-face, medium nose
describe.B: long / narrow: high close-set eyes, long nose, low mouth, long cleft chin
describe.C: broad: wide-set low eyes under a heavy two-row brow, broad nose, wide mouth, jowls, square jaw
describe.D: round / young: short chubby face, big dark eyes, high thin brows, button nose, small high mouth, round cheeks
describe.E: gaunt: deep-set shaded eye sockets, high cheekbones over hollow cheeks, hook nose, thin low mouth, long chin

faces.rule: no two roles next to each other in a town cast (data/townsfolk.js CAST_BY_TOWN, for every official faction and every sweetheart gender / fallback) share a structure; nor do neighbours in the rev 1 atlas block. verify.py: adjacentSameFace

suitorGender.why: the generic rev 1 sweetheart read as female; rev 2 has pt-suitor-f (that art), pt-suitor-m (new) and pt-suitor (new, neutral fallback)
suitorGender.gameToday: no gender field: data/world.js CITIES[town].suitor fixes three named sweethearts; every other town names its sweetheart from TOWN_FIRST via a seeded hash (systems/townsfolk.js drawCast)
suitorGender.pick: gender = n.gender ?? SUITOR_GENDER[n.town] ?? firstNameGender of n.name.split(' ')[0] ?? null
suitorGender.lookupNote: insert the two -<g> steps into portraitKeys() for role suitor when the gender is known; with no gender the current lookup (pt-<town>-suitor, pt-suitor) still works and shows the neutral pt-suitor in the 8 unnamed towns
suitorGender.spriteNote: only the three named towns can be married into today (city.js uses CITIES[town].suitor), so the per-home sprite always exists; the -f / -m / neutral generic sprites are the fallback for any future town

pairs.rule: a sweetheart portrait and the home sprite of the same person wear the same outfit colours and carry the same key prop (both are built from src/people/looks.py LOOKS)
pairs.check: dominant clothing keys (>= 15% of the clothing pixels; K, skin and hair excluded) of the portrait chest (figure layer, rows 34-46, x13-35) vs the sprite torso (idle frame 4, rows 11-15): the main key of each must be among the other's keys (>= 5%), and they must share a dominant key; the prop key (props) must show on both

ashfordBoards.sampledFrom: screenshots/96b, 96c, 96d (Ashford wagon boards behind the home sprites)
ashfordBoards.fix: Edda (portrait + sprite): brown dress -> woad blue (B, K shade, u highlight) with a white apron; CIE76 dE of every dominant outfit key vs D and O must be >= 40

integration: portraits: load each pt-* PNG as an image texture under its key (or slice portraits-atlas.png by `order`). Lookup: pt-<town>-<role>, pt-<role>-<faction>, pt-<role> (unchanged); for role suitor insert the gender steps (portraits.suitorGender.lookup) once the game knows the gender.

rev 2 town variants: every town now has pt-<town>-innkeeper and pt-<town>-merchant (pt-sinkroot-merchant is reserved: the dungeon cast has no merchant). The three named towns keep pt-<town>-suitor; the eight others have pt-<town>-suitor-f and pt-<town>-suitor-m (no ungendered town key, so today they fall back to the neutral pt-suitor).

suitor gender: no gender field exists. Suggested: give CITIES[town].suitor a gender (ashford f, millbrook m, oakwatch f) and derive the rest from the first name (portraits.suitorGender.firstNameGender, covers all 22 TOWN_FIRST names); then portraitKeys(n) for suitors = [pt-<town>-suitor-<g>, pt-<town>-suitor, pt-suitor-<g>, pt-suitor] and spouseKeys = [w8-fam-spouse[-babe]-<home>, w8-fam-spouse[-babe]-<g>, w8-fam-spouse[-babe]].

tests/people-rules.mjs (game side) will need three edits for rev 2: (1) mossmarket innkeeper now resolves to pt-mossmarket-innkeeper, not pt-innkeeper; (2) "every portrait is drawn for someone" must allow the gendered / reserved keys until the gender step lands (pt-suitor-f/-m, pt-<town>-suitor-f/-m, pt-sinkroot-merchant); (3) the sprite key regex must accept w8-fam-spouse[-babe]-f|m.
business icons: in businessPanel replace the letter box with w8-biz-<kind>-32 at (x+3, y+3) inside the existing 38 px box, or w8-biz-<kind> at 2x.

HUD: w8-hud-roost next to "Nightglass roost", w8-hud-informant next to "Informants", w8-hud-postrider next to "Post-riders"; w8-hud-gate-<done> beside gateLine() on the Month tab / HUD and in the Progress panel title (rev 2 art, same keys and states).

home sprites: CityScene draws the spouse with ensurePerson8(this, "spouse", gear) at (128,136); to use P9 swap in w8-fam-spouse[-<home town>] (anchor x8 y21, origin (0.5,1)); gear overlays are not drawn on the P9 spouse (it has no layer split). When fam.children has a babe and the spouse is home, use w8-fam-spouse-babe[-<town>] instead; children by childStage(age): child -> w8-fam-child-a|b, youth -> w8-fam-youth-a|b, babe (if not held) -> w8-fam-babe-a|b placed on the ground by the house.
Phaser anims: walk = frames 0-3 at 8 fps, idle = 4-7 at 4 fps; cradle idle = 0-3 at 3 fps. Load strips with this.load.spritesheet(key, file, {frameWidth: 16, frameHeight: 22}).
